items.claim: The onset seam at 16:50/16:51 carries no device of the book's prophetic frame on either face. 16:50 ends וָאָסִ֥יר אֶתְהֶ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי (oshb:Ezek.16.50) with no close signature, and the row's own onset sentence grants that 16:51 carries no onset device and continues the comparative indictment, so the seam is held by the setumah the witness places after 16:50 and by nothing else. Two byte-true arcs cross it. The sister-pair announced at 16:46 is treated member by member, Sodom in 16:48-50 and Samaria at 16:51 in וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה (oshb:Ezek.16.51); and the bearing-of-shame arc that this row's own close completes begins one verse later, at גַּם אַ֣תְּ שְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֗ךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.52), is restated as a purpose clause at לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.54), and ends in the perfect at אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58). As shipped, the span opens inside the comparison and carries Samaria's member into the shame movement, which is two movements in one row.
items.both_sides: Close side of the seam: nothing at 16:50 closes a unit - no recognition, no utterance, no spoken signature - and the oath-and-utterance pair חַי אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.48) stands at the head of 16:48, opening Sodom's paragraph rather than closing anything, so 16:48-50 is Sodom's member of the pair announced at 16:46. Onset side: the fronted subject in וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה does open Samaria's member, which is real paragraph-level evidence, but that member answers 16:48-50 and shares the comparative vocabulary of 16:47 and 16:50 across the seam, so it argues continuity with what precedes. At 16:52 the two arcs meet: the verse both renders the comparison's verdict and issues the shame imperative that 16:54 and 16:58 carry to its end. That is why the paragraph mark and the lexical arcs point one verse apart, and why a medium confidence is the honest posture at either placement. The verse this row argues without carrying it in its evidence list, 16:59, is a rival-theory anchor and not boundary evidence for this seam.

suggested_fix.fact: the bearing-of-shame arc that this row closes opens at 16:52 with the imperative, is restated as a purpose clause at 16:54, and ends in the perfect at 16:58 where the witness also sets a setumah; Samaria's member of the sister-pair at 16:51 answers Sodom's at 16:48-50 under the pair announced at 16:46

items.claim: The unit is device-bounded on both faces, and its internal refrain is correctly read as paragraph-final rather than row-final. The messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59) opens 16:59; the second-person recognition form וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.62) stands at 16:62, one of the five verses the formula census counts for that form; and 16:63 opens with the purpose clause לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.63), which makes that verse grammatically dependent on the covenant establishment it follows, so the row's close at the long utterance signature נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.63) is the unit's real terminus. The turn from the sisters' indictment to remembered covenant also carries the category deviation the row discloses.
items.both_sides: Close side of the onset seam: 16:58 ends in the short-form signature and the witness sets a setumah after it, so the far face of this row's onset is a genuine close. Onset side: a messenger formula opening a first-person covenant speech, with the addressee's burden turning from accusation to restoration. Close side of the row's own end: the long utterance signature at 16:63, with a setumah and the chapter's end; its far face is the word-event onset at 17:1. Both seams therefore carry devices on both faces, which is what makes the internal refrain at 16:62 the weaker of the two candidate closes rather than the row's end.

suggested_fix.fact: 16:63 opens with a purpose clause and is therefore grammatically dependent on the covenant establishment at 16:62; that dependency, rather than the relative strength of the two signatures, is the ground on which the second-person recognition at 16:62 is paragraph-final

items.claim: The riddle runs from a first-order onset to a seam that is first-order on its far face. 17:1 carries the word-event onset and 17:2 names the genre with both the riddle term and the parable term; the row's close at 17:10 in תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ (oshb:Ezek.17.10) answers the riddle's own rhetorical question; and the next verse is the word-event onset וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.17.11), a 37-character verse whose bytes are identical to those of 17:1, so the seam at 17:10/17:11 is carried by a text device and not by the petuchah alone. The interior setumah after 17:8 is rightly declined: the speech command אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.17.9) keeps the same addressee and the same vine, and a messenger formula with no addressee change and no close behind it opens a paragraph, not a row.
items.both_sides: Close side of the onset seam: 16:63 carries the long utterance signature, the chapter's end and a setumah. Onset side: the word-event at 17:1 with the riddle-and-parable command at 17:2. Close side of the row's own end: 17:10 completes the riddle's answer, with a petuchah after the verse. Onset side of that seam: 17:11, the word-event onset verse, byte-identical to 17:1. Of the verses this row argues without mirroring them in its evidence list, 17:12-24 are rival-span anchors, but 17:11 is load-bearing - it is the far face of this row's own closing seam and belongs in the evidence the row names.

suggested_fix.fact: the far face of this row's closing seam is the word-event onset at 17:11, whose bytes are identical to the onset at 17:1, so the seam is carried by a first-order device on both faces and not by the petuchah at 17:10

items.claim: The row's close at 17:18 leaves the word-event unit it opens without its refrain. 17:18 ends in לֹ֥א יִמָּלֵֽט (oshb:Ezek.17.18), a content-final clause with no close signature, while the refrain that closes what the word-event at 17:11 opens stands three verses later at וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.17.21) - the second-person-plural recognition stacked with the spoken signature, corroborated by a setumah. The device the seam is cut on, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי אָנִי֒ (oshb:Ezek.17.19), is a therefore-clause with the messenger formula and the oath; that same oath device already stands verse-initially inside this row's own span at חַי אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.17.16) and is rightly not cut there, which fixes it as a verdict-paragraph opener in this unit rather than a row onset. One seam, two rows: the unit is 17:11-21, eleven verses.
items.both_sides: Close side (17:18): no recognition, no utterance, no spoken signature; the clause completes the account of the broken oath, and the setumah after the verse is single-witness paragraph evidence, which informs a seam and cannot decide one by itself. Onset side (17:19): a therefore-clause plus the messenger formula plus the oath - and in this book the oath is an emphatic sub-onset of a verdict paragraph, never a row onset on its own, while a messenger formula opens a row only where the addressee changes or a close stands immediately before it. Neither condition holds: the addressee is unchanged from 17:12 onward and 17:18 carries no close. The verses this row argues without mirroring them (17:1, 17:19-21) are the comparison of two identical onsets and the rival span, not independent boundary evidence.

suggested_fix.fact: the recognition-and-spoken refrain at 17:21 closes the word-event unit opened at 17:11, and the oath at 17:19 repeats the oath already standing at 17:16 inside this span

items.claim: The onset at 17:19 is not carried by a licensed onset device: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי אָנִי֒ (oshb:Ezek.17.19) is a therefore-clause with the messenger formula and the oath, the addressee is unchanged from 17:12-18, no close signature stands at 17:18, and the identical oath device stands verse-initially at חַי אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.17.16) without opening a row there. The material is the verdict paragraph of the unit the word-event at 17:11 opens, whose refrain close וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.17.21) is this row's own last verse. A second fact bears on the confidence: the two spans that share the 17:18/17:19 seam carry different confidences, the span ending at 17:18 medium and this three-verse span high, and the higher of the two is the one whose onset is that seam.
items.both_sides: Onset side (17:19): a paragraph-grade opener - therefore-clause, messenger formula, oath - repeating the oath of 17:16. Close side of that seam (17:18): content-final, no close signature, only the setumah. Close side of the row's own end (17:21): second-person-plural recognition plus the spoken signature plus a setumah, a genuine refrain; and its far face at 17:22 is a fresh messenger formula, licensed there precisely because 17:21 closes. So this row's closing seam is sound and its opening seam is not, which is the asymmetry a single high confidence cannot express. The verses argued but unmirrored here (17:22-24) are the rival merge, not boundary evidence.

items.claim: Both seams are device-carried on both faces. The onset כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.17.22) is a fresh messenger formula standing immediately after the refrain close at 17:21, which is one of the two conditions under which a messenger formula opens a row in this book. The close at 17:24 is refrain-grade twice over: וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל עֲצֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Ezek.17.24) is a recognition clause with an expanded subject, and the verse then ends in אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִֽׂיתִי (oshb:Ezek.17.24), the spoken signature extended by the promise to act, with a petuchah and the chapter's end coinciding. The row names only the second of those two close devices.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the messenger formula at 17:22 opening a first-person planting figure. Close side of that seam: 17:21's recognition plus spoken signature, a refrain that closes the unit before it, with a setumah after the verse. Close side of the row's own end: the doubled close at 17:24 with a petuchah; its far face is the word-event onset at 18:1. Both faces of both seams therefore carry first-order devices, which is what supports the high confidence. The verses argued but unmirrored here (16:59-63, 17:3, 17:11) are the rejected-category comparison and the figure's earlier occurrence, not boundary evidence.

items.claim: Two facts, neither of which moves the span. First, the ground stated for declining the alternative that runs to 18:9 is the setumah at 18:4 - a single-witness paragraph mark set against a genuine close signature, since 18:9 ends in חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.9), the utterance formula, which the row names only as the rival span's last verse without naming the device it carries. The first-order ground for the shipped division is available and unused: the case opened at וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק (oshb:Ezek.18.5) is the first of a series of parallel cases, each closed by its own signature, so folding it into the thesis would join two signed movements. Second, the oath-and-utterance pair at 18:3 is described as standing mid-verse, but the bytes place it verse-initially - חַי אָ֕נִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה is the opening of 18:3 (oshb:Ezek.18.3) - which is also the reason it is onset-side texture for the prohibition that follows rather than a close.
items.both_sides: Close side (18:4): the thesis הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) is content-complete and the witness sets a setumah after the verse, but there is no close signature. Onset side (18:5): a casuistic protasis, which is not among this book's onset devices, so the seam is carried by the mark plus a shift of genre from disputation address to case law. The seam holds - but on the ground that the case which follows is itself closed by the utterance formula at 18:9 and so cannot be absorbed into the thesis, not on the ground the row states, since a paragraph mark informs a seam and never decides one. The two verses this row argues without mirroring them, 18:5 and 18:9, are exactly the two that carry this evidence.

suggested_fix.fact: the case opened at 18:5 is closed by the utterance formula at 18:9, which is why the thesis and the first case are two signed movements; and the oath with the utterance at 18:3 stands verse-initially, not mid-verse
